The runway is three months long. The optimism is infinite.
The build has been running for nine minutes. Everyone pretends not to watch.
The oldest TODO is load bearing. Nobody dares touch it. It is holding up the building.
And here, in the glow of the monitor, we observe the vibe coder in its natural habitat.

The post drifts through the new queue, unseen, unloved, and strangely dignified.
This one quit a stable job. It owns forty thousand dollars, a garage, and no plan.

The database, for the record, has been gone since the first day. Nobody noticed. The app works anyway. Mostly.

A new AI model is announced. Everyone agrees it changes everything. Everyone goes back to work.

In the kitchen, the snacks are depleted. The staff regard this as a human rights issue.
The pager sleeps. The senior developer does not trust it. He watches it, like a snake.
Tokens are consumed. Somewhere, a data center warms its hands on the founder's ambition.
Many weeks later, the app was shipped. Nobody could say how.
The bot replied to itself. Then to its own reply. This has continued for three days.
The standup has lasted forty minutes. Nobody has stood.
On Monday, it shipped without incident. The senior developer was seen smiling. The staff were frightened.
The balance is dangerously low. The founder responds as founders do: by posting about gratitude.
Little does the founder know, the database is already gone.
The cat does not apply. The cat has already committed to main.
Three days later, the model replied. It said: hello. The laptop has never been the same.
A cat appears. It looks at the team. It looks at the code. It chooses the sofa.
A coder in the wild deletes a failing test. He calls it a refactor. Nature is cruel.
The intern arrives early, clutching a coffee and a dream. The coffee is stronger.
It walked across the keyboard. Fourteen files changed. Nobody dares revert.
The team chat lights up with forty messages. Nobody has said anything. This is called alignment.
And so it shipped, on a Friday, against all advice. In a distant room, a pager cleared its throat.
The vibe coder says he will fix it in a minute. In the wild, a minute can last a quarter.
The office plant dies. It was the last employee with a work life balance.
And here we observe the loading spinner. It has been spinning since Tuesday. It has started a family.
I trained a model on your feelings. It is cautiously optimistic.
The founder has an idea in the shower. By noon, it is the strategy. By evening, a pivot.
The cat considers the list. The cat sits on the list. The list is now complete.
The senior developer sighs. It is the sound of a thousand merged pull requests.
The espresso machine breaks. Productivity halves. Morale does not recover. This is how empires end.
The vibe coder types: fix it. He does not say what. The machine understands.
The cloud bill arrives. It is, once again, for a service nobody remembers turning on.
In a glass room, the founder meets the money. The money is wearing a vest.
A merge conflict emerges. Two creatures face each other across the same four lines. Neither will yield.
The cat sits on the warm laptop. This is its code review.
